Historian Daniele Bolelli joins Joe Rogan for episode 357 of the Joe Rogan Experience, an early entry in the show's long run. Bolelli is a writer and teacher who tells history as a string of wild human tales. His style fits the young show well.

Bolelli and Rogan roam from samurai codes to fallen empires and mad kings. The talk has the loose, late-night feel of the show's first years. Rogan lets the tales run and jumps in with his own loves: fights, hunts, and hard men. Listeners get storyteller history at full length. The library keeps the episode as a record of the show's early form.

Cryptographer Moxie Marlinspike joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1572. Marlinspike built Signal, the encrypted messaging app used by millions, and he has strong views on privacy as a right that must be engineered, not requested. Rogan, wary of surveillance, is a natural host for him.

He explains how Signal keeps messages sealed, why metadata matters, and what governments keep asking tech firms to build. Rogan asks what privacy a normal person can still hold. The episode is a rare long talk with a quiet, radical builder whose work sits in more pockets than almost any other guest's.
